name: add_u8_capped
proto: void add_u8_capped(u8 *value /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int amount /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, unsigned max /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Saturating byte add: if *value + amount < max then *value += amount, otherwise *value = max (so the result never exceeds max; reaching exactly max also clamps). Used for counters such as the moongate height (475a: add_u8_capped(&g_moongate_height,1,16)), stats, item counts (callers in CMDS/SHOPPES/SJOG/TALK/OUTSUBS and end_of_turn_party_update).

name: add_i16_capped
proto: void add_i16_capped(int *value /*param_3*/, int amount /*param_2*/, int max /*param_1*/)
purpose: Signed 16-bit version of add_u8_capped: *value = (*value+amount < max) ? *value+amount : max. Used for hit points (regeneration_ring_tick: add_i16_capped(&hp,1,max_hp)), experience, gold etc.

name: sub_u8_floor
purpose: Saturating byte subtract: if amount < *value then *value -= amount else *value = 0. Used for torch/light-spell turn counters in pass_time, the moongate height in update_moongates, hours-until-heal, etc.

name: sub_i16_floor
purpose: Signed 16-bit version of sub_u8_floor: *value = (amount < *value) ? *value-amount : 0. Used for food/gold/hp decrements by COMBAT, SHOPPES, TALK and end_of_turn_party_update.

name: view_tile_missile_passable
purpose: Looks up the terrain tile currently in the 11x11 view buffer at (row,col) (g_view_tiles[row*0x20+col]) and tests its bit in the 256-bit table g_missile_pass_bitmap (bit = 0x80>>(tile&7) of byte tile>>3). Returns nonzero when the bit is SET. In the DATA.OVL table the bit is clear for mountains/peaks (0x0c,0x0d), the settlement icons 0x12-0x15 and 0x19-0x1b, castle tiles 0x3a-0x3f, mast 0x42, pillar 0x46, stone walls 0x4d-0x4f, crenellations 0x50-0x55, window shelf 0x5a, 'strange walls' 0x70-0x7f, doors 0xb8/0xb9 and the collapsed dungeon entrance 0xdf, i.e. solid things a projectile/spell cannot pass; windows, arrow slits, water, trees pass. Only used by CAST (db30) and COMSUBS (f4be), i.e. for ranged attacks/spell lines of fire. Note: it tests the VIEW buffer (0 where an object sits), not the map.

0xab02.name: g_view_tiles
0xab02.meaning: terrain tile of each view cell (row stride 0x20); 0 = an object is drawn there instead (see g_view_objects), 0xff = darkness

0x6a14.name: g_missile_pass_bitmap
0x6a14.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a24: one bit per tile 0..255, set = projectiles/spell effects can pass through this tile

notes: Game meaning of the bitmap inferred from which tiles are clear; the two callers are in CAST/COMSUBS.

name: pixel_to_view_cell
purpose: Converts a screen pixel position inside the map view (8..183 in both axes, i.e. the 11x11 cells of 16px starting at pixel 8) into a view cell: g_dx = (px-8)/16, g_dy = (py-8)/16 (truncating signed division). If either coordinate is outside 8..0xb7 both g_dx and g_dy are set to -1. Callers: CAST db30 and COMSUBS f4be (targeting of spells/missiles, same pair as view_tile_missile_passable).

name: regeneration_ring_tick
purpose: For every party member (0..g_party_count-1) whose status is not 'D' (dead) and whose ring slot (record+0x1d) holds item 44 = ',' (Regeneration Ring), rolls rand_range(0,7) and on a 7 (1 in 8) heals 1 HP: add_i16_capped(&hp(+0x10), 1, max_hp(+0x12)) and sets g_status_dirty. Called from end_of_turn_party_update (2ae8), CMDS, SHOPPES3 and ROOT 6794.

0x55c5.name: g_party_ring
0x55c5.meaning: party record +0x1d ring item (',' = 44 = Regeneration Ring), stride 0x20

name: set_active_player
purpose: Implements the digit keys of the main loops (callers DUNGEON 8894, MAINOUT 8c54, TOWN 9004). Prints 'Set Active Plr:\n'. key '0' (0x30): prints 'None!' and sets g_active_member = 0xff. Otherwise idx = key-'1'; if idx >= g_party_count or that member's status is 'D' (dead) or 'S' (asleep): prints 'Invalid!' and returns 1 (nothing changed, no status redraw). Otherwise g_active_member = idx, the member's name (record at 0x55a8+idx*0x20) is printed followed by a newline. In both successful cases draw_status_window() is called and 0 returned.

name: play_ambient_sounds
purpose: Called once per animation frame from refresh_map_view (5910) when animation is on. Scans the 11x11 cells around the party (map coords px-5..px+5, py-5..py+5; in combat, loc>=0x80, centre 5,5) and finds the NEAREST (squared distance, initial best 0x33) sound source, examining the MAP tile via get_map_tile(x,y): tiles 0xfa/0xfb (grandfather clock) -> type 1; 0xd4-0xd7 (waterfall) -> type 2; 0xd8-0xdb (unnamed animated tiles, almost certainly a fountain) -> type 3; a view cell holding an object (g_view_tiles==0) whose object tile is 0x15c-0x15f (the second 'minstrel' set = a musician) -> type 4. Then plays: type 1 (clock): if no chimes are pending (g_clock_chimes==0) or the frame counter g_ambient_frame is not 0 or 4, it ticks: beep(3000Hz,3) on frame 0, beep(2000Hz,3) on frame 4, nothing on other frames; if chimes are pending and the frame is 0 or 4 it plays a chime play_sweep_noise(phase_step=0xc2c,hold=1,count=2000,threshold=20000,threshold_step=-10) and (at the end) decrements g_clock_chimes. Type 2: play_random_tones(step=0x14,total=0x3c,max_freq=10000) (rushing water). Type 3: play_random_tones(10,0x1e,25000). Type 4: note = g_tune_sequence[g_tune_pos]; if nonzero plays play_sweep_noise(phase_step=g_tune_notes word at 0x6a34+2*note, hold=1,count=2000,threshold=20000,step=-10); then g_tune_pos++ wrapping to 0 after 0x34 (a 53-note loop; 0 = rest). Finally g_ambient_frame = (g_ambient_frame+1) & 7-ish (reset to 0 when >7). Ghidra shows the frequency constants as bogus string pointers (s__Have_a_pleasant_night_+0xd = 20000, s_Missed_+1 = 10000, 0x61a8 = 25000).

0xac64.name: g_view_objects
0xac64.meaning: object/NPC tile (0x100-relative) drawn at each view cell when g_view_tiles is 0 (row stride 0x10)

0x5884.name: g_clock_chimes
0x5884.meaning: save 0x2DE: number of clock strikes still to sound (set to hour mod 12, 12 at 0h, by pass_time on each hour change)

0x6a34.name: g_ambient_frame
0x6a34.meaning: ambient-sound frame counter 0..7 (the words at 0x6a36.. following it are the tune note table)

0x6a36.name: g_tune_notes
0x6a36.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a46: 9 note frequencies/phase steps 0x0da9..0x1b53 indexed 1..9 by g_tune_sequence (word index n is at 0x6a34+2n)

0x6a48.name: g_tune_sequence
0x6a48.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a58: the musician's 53-note tune, 0 = rest, 1..9 = note index

0x6a08.name: g_tune_pos
0x6a08.meaning: current position in g_tune_sequence (0..0x34), RAM counter just after the map buffer

notes: Tile 0xd8-0xdb identity (fountain) is inferred: LOOK2.DAT names them '*'. Clock tick/tock at frames 0/4 of an 8-frame cycle.

name: play_footstep_sound
purpose: Two short random-tone bursts separated by a delay: play_random_tones(step=1,total=25,max_freq=1000); delay_loop(speed_index=1,count=20); play_random_tones(1,25,1500). TOWN calls it when the party moves on foot (g_transport_tile==0x1c) or on horseback (0x12/0x13); MAINOUT, BLCKTHRN, SJOG, ENDGAME, CAST2 use it for the same step sound.

name: play_triple_sweep_sound
purpose: Plays play_sweep_noise(phase_step=4600,hold=1,count=10800,threshold=300,threshold_step=6) three times, then play_sweep_noise(6100,1,21600,300,3) once (a longer final sweep). Ghidra shows the numeric arguments as bogus string pointers. Callers: CAST d534 and the COMBAT main loop ae24 - a spell/combat fanfare whose exact game meaning was not determined.
notes: Which event triggers it must be read from CAST/COMBAT.

name: play_tone_sweep
proto: void play_tone_sweep(unsigned start_freq /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, unsigned end_freq /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int step /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int total /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Linear frequency glide on the PC speaker: for i = 0; i < total; i += step: start_tone(freq); delay_loop(speed_index=1,count=step); freq += (end_freq-start_freq)*step/total. Then stop_tone(). Used all over (CAST, CMDS, COMBAT, COMSUBS, DUNGEON, MAINOUT, SJOG, TALK, ZSTATS, ROOT 6936) for rising/falling effect sounds.

name: get_map_tile
purpose: Returns a pointer to the map byte for map coordinates (x,y) in the current map buffer; callers read or write through it. Three cases on g_location: (a) 0 = overworld (Britannia/Underworld): x -= g_chunk_x, y -= g_chunk_y, both masked & 0x1f, giving a position inside the 32x32 window of 4 cached 16x16 chunks at g_map (0x6608): chunk index c = (y>=16 ? 2 : 0) + (x>=16 ? 1 : 0) (coords reduced mod 16), address = 0x6608 + c*0x100 + (y&15)*16 + (x&15) - i.e. chunks are top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, each row-major 16x16 (the masking means coordinates wrap around the 256x256 world and the cache window). (b) 1..0x7f = town/dungeon level: if x or y is outside 0..31 returns the address of the last map byte 0x6a07 (map[31][31], used as the out-of-bounds filler); else 0x6608 + y*32 + x (the 32x32 map, save-RAM offset 0x1062). (c) >=0x80 = combat: returns g_light_map + y*0x20 + x (the combat map lives at 0xad14 with stride 32, no bounds check). 70 callers across all modules.

0x589b.name: g_chunk_x
0x589b.meaning: save 0x2F5: world x of the top-left cached chunk (multiple of 16); 0 in towns

0x589c.name: g_chunk_y
0x589c.meaning: save 0x2F6: world y of the top-left cached chunk

0x6608.name: g_map
0x6608.meaning: RAM 0x1062 past the save image: current 32x32 town/dungeon-level map (row-major) or the 4 cached overworld chunks (4 x 16x16, order TL,TR,BL,BR)

0x6a07.name: g_map_last_cell
0x6a07.meaning: map[31][31]; returned for out-of-range town coordinates

0xad14.name: g_light_map
0xad14.meaning: RAM: in towns the light map built by rebuild_light_map (0 = unlit, else the tile); in combat (loc>=0x80) the 11x11 combat map (stride 0x20)

name: cycle_tile_anim_map
purpose: Advances the terrain animation remap table g_tile_anim_map (256 bytes, entry t = tile actually drawn for map tile t). Every call: entries 0xd4..0xd7 (waterfall) are incremented and wrapped back to 0xd4 when they reach 0xd8; entries 0xd8..0xdb (fountain) likewise wrap at 0xdc. On every second call (g_anim_frame_counter bit 0 set): entries 0x80..0x83 (pendulum) are XORed with 1 (swing), entries 0xec..0xef (standard of Britannia) cycle within 0xec..0xef; and on every fourth call (bit 1 also set) entries 0xfa..0xfd (grandfather clock, bellows) are XORed with 1. Then g_anim_frame_counter++. Called only from animate_monsters (4552), i.e. once per animated frame. The initial table in DATA.OVL is all zero; something at start-up (part 4 / overlay code) must fill it with the identity mapping.

0xb11e.name: g_tile_anim_map
0xb11e.meaning: display tile for each terrain tile 0..255 (identity except the animated groups); used by draw_map_view

0x6a7e.name: g_anim_frame_counter
0x6a7e.meaning: frame counter for terrain animation (bit0 = every 2nd frame, bit1 = every 4th)

name: animate_monsters
purpose: Per-frame sprite animation of every non-empty slot of g_monster_table (32 x 8 bytes), driven by the slot's byte +6 (Value 2): low nibble = delay counter (0xf = frozen, never animates), high nibble = position in an animation script. base = tile0 & 0xfc (the 4-frame group); script row = g_anim_script_index[(base-0x34)>>2] (one byte per tile group from 0x134 upward; e.g. guards->5, sharks->9, bats/ghosts/slimes/orcs/pythons/headless/daemons->1, spiders->6, mimics->4, gazers->3, gargoyles->10, dragons/trolls->7, mongbats->2, corpsers->8, most others 0). If the delay nibble is nonzero it is just decremented. If it is 0 the slot animates only when: anim tile (+1) is not 0, 0x1d or 0x1e, base > 0x33 (objects, vehicles and chairs below 0x134 never animate), base != 0xe8 (fields), base != 0xb4 (shards/crown/sceptre/amulet), and (base == 0x5c (musician) or base == 0xa8 (mimic chest) or rand_range(0,255) >= 0x80 i.e. 50%). It then interprets g_anim_scripts[row][pos] in a loop: 1..4 -> anim tile = base+cmd-1, pos++, stop; 5 -> 75%: pos++ and continue; 25%: anim tile = tile0 (frame 0), then for the musician pos++ and stop, else keep pos and set delay 6, stop; 6 -> 25%: pos++ continue, 75%: fall into 0; 0 -> pos = 0, continue; 7 -> pos = 2, continue; any other (0x80|n) -> delay = n (cmd+0x80 as a byte), pos++, stop. The new state byte is pos*16+delay. After the loop over all 32 slots it calls cycle_tile_anim_map (44b8) and ROOT 6fd6 (driver entry 32 with CF=0, AX=g_font_segs[0] - the driver-side part of the per-frame animation, see part 4). Callers: refresh_map_view, CAST2 e64c, FONT e4dc.

0x5c5a.name: g_monster_table
0x5c5a.meaning: save 0x6B4 monster/object table: +0 tile, +1 anim tile, +2 x, +3 y, +4 z, +5 value1, +6 value2 (animation state: hi nibble script pos, lo nibble delay, 0xf frozen), +7 value3

0x1b18.name: g_anim_scripts
0x1b18.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x1b28: 11 animation scripts of up to 16 commands (1-4 frame, 5/6 random, 0 restart, 7 goto 2, 0x80|n wait n)

0x1bc8.name: g_anim_script_index
0x1bc8.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x1bd8: script row for each 4-tile group from 0x134 ((tile&0xfc)-0x34)/4

notes: Driver call happens inside 6fd6 (part 4). Random gates use rand_range(0,255).

name: moonstone_on_current_map
purpose: Returns 1 if moonstone index (0..7) is buried on the map the party is on: g_moonstone_loc[index] == g_location and g_moonstone_z[index] == g_party_z, and additionally in the overworld (location 0) its x/y must lie inside the 32x32 cached chunk window ((u8)(x - g_chunk_x) < 0x20 and (u8)(y - g_chunk_y) < 0x20). Otherwise 0. A moonstone carried in inventory has loc 0xff so never matches. Only caller: update_moongates.

0x5840.name: g_moonstone_loc
0x5840.meaning: save 0x29A: location code where the stone is buried (0 = Britannia/Underworld map), 0xff = in inventory

0x5848.name: g_moonstone_z
0x5848.meaning: save 0x2A2: z/level where buried (0 Britannia, 0xff Underworld)

name: update_moongates
purpose: Called every animated frame (from refresh_map_view, non-combat). Decides the moongate tile: by day (5 <= g_hour < 20) g_moongate_height is decremented (floor 0) and the tile is 0xdc (moon gate) while height > 0, or 5 (grass) once it has shrunk to 0; at night the height is incremented up to 16 and the tile is 0xdc. Then for each of the 8 moonstones that moonstone_on_current_map reports as buried here, writes that tile into the map at (x,y) via get_map_tile, ORs 2 into g_view_dirty, and if the map byte actually changed calls rebuild_light_map (5e4a; a moongate is a light source). So all buried moonstones become moongates at night and the gates visibly grow/shrink over 16 frames; draw_map_view renders a partial gate while 1 <= height <= 15.

0x5887.name: g_moongate_height
0x5887.meaning: save 0x2E1: moongate height 0..16 (frames of the rise/shrink animation)

0x24e6.name: g_view_dirty
0x24e6.meaning: map view must be rebuilt (bit 1 OR'ed here)

name: moongate_travel
purpose: Teleports the party to the burial place of moonstone number `moonstone` (0..7, chosen from the moon phase). Returns 0 immediately if that stone is in inventory (g_moonstone_loc == 0xff). If the party is currently in the overworld: select_disk(1), wait until BRIT.DAT exists, and save the monster table (0x100 bytes at g_monster_table) to the overworld object file named by OUTSUBS a5f8 ('BRIT.OOL' when g_party_z==0 else 'UNDER.OOL'). Sets g_party_x/y/z from the stone. Then: if both the destination loc and the current loc are settlements (1..0x20): g_location = dest and TOWN_93c0(1) loads/initialises that town; if both are 0 (overworld, incl. Britannia<->Underworld via z): g_location = 0, loads the monster table back from the .OOL file for the new level (load_file_region(name, g_monster_table, 0x100, 0)) and MAINOUT_81d0 reloads the chunk cache; any other combination just keeps g_location and the new coordinates (not expected in practice). Returns 1. Callers: enter_moongate (48a8) and CAST cc70.

name: enter_moongate
purpose: Called by the MAINOUT and TOWN main loops after a move. If the map tile under the party is 0xdc (moon gate): animate_wait(1); play_sweep_noise(5900,1,2000,20000,2) (teleport sound); temporarily sets g_transport_tile = 0x16 (sprite 0x116, a blank - so the party is not drawn) and runs tile_transition_effect(0xdc, 5, 5) (dissolve of the gate at the centre cell), then g_transport_tile = 0, animate_wait(1), and shrinks the gate with draw_effect_frame(h,5,5) for h = 15 down to 1 with wait_ticks(2) between frames. The map byte at the party position is set to 5 (grass), g_view_dirty |= 2, draw_tile(5,5,5). Then: if g_hour == 0 and g_minute < 10 (first ten minutes after midnight) it restores the transport tile and returns 1 (the caller then performs the special midnight destination via FUN_1778_02ea); otherwise phase = g_trammel_phase if hour < 12 else g_felucca_phase (characters '0'..'7'), moongate_travel(phase-'0'), restore the transport tile, return 0. Returns 0 when not standing on a gate.

0x587c.name: g_transport_tile
0x587c.meaning: party sprite -0x100 (0x1c foot); 0x16 = blank while the gate dissolves

0x5885.name: g_trammel_phase
0x5885.meaning: save 0x2DF phase of Trammel '0'..'7' (destination moonstone for hours 0-11)

0x5886.name: g_felucca_phase
0x5886.meaning: save 0x2E0 phase of Felucca '0'..'7' (destination for hours 12-23)

notes: The wiki says Trammel applies for hours 0-4 and Felucca 20-23; the code simply splits at noon. Midnight special case handled by the caller.

name: select_target_member
purpose: Returns the party member index a command applies to (used by SJOG/LOOKOBJ/DNGLOOK/CAST for Jimmy, Use, Get, spells...). In combat (g_location >= 0x81) it is simply the party index stored in the combat roster entry of the active combatant (g_combat_roster[g_active_combatant].+3). Otherwise: if g_active_member != 0xff return it. Else count members with status 'G' or 'P' (remembering the last one): if 0 -> result -1 (0xffff) and prints 'None!'; if exactly 1 -> that member silently; if several -> loop: print 'Player: ', select_party_member_no_zero(); a negative answer (-1 Esc / -2) ends the loop and is returned (-2 prints a newline); a 'G'/'P' member is accepted and its name printed (plus a newline if the cursor column is not 0); a dead/asleep member prints 'Disabled!' and asks again.

0x589e.name: g_active_combatant
0x589e.meaning: index of the combatant whose turn it is

0xba17.name: g_roster_member
0xba17.meaning: g_combat_roster entry +3: party member index for party-side entries (monster type for monsters), stride 8

name: draw_sky_strip
purpose: Draws the sun/moons indicator on the top screen row. Does nothing in dungeons (g_location > 0x20). Builds a 12-character string of spaces: the sun '*' at index 17-g_hour if 0..11 (so the sun is at the right end at 6h and the left end at 17h, i.e. rises in the east); g_trammel_phase = g_moon_phase_table[day][0] placed at index (8-hour) mod 24 if < 12; g_felucca_phase = g_moon_phase_table[day][1] at index (2-hour) mod 24 if < 12 (both characters are the phase glyphs '0'..'7' in font 1). Selects window 0 and font 1, cursor at column 6 row 0. In Ararat (location 0x19) or when g_party_z >= 0x80 (Underworld/basement) it instead fills pixels x 40..152, y 0..6 with g_ui_color2 and draws a line at y=7 in g_ui_color1 (no sky). Otherwise prints each character with set_text_color(g_ui_color_sun) for '*' and g_ui_color_moon for anything else, then restores g_ui_color1, the previous window and font 0. Called by pass_time on each hour change and by the map loaders.

0x1ed8.name: g_moon_phase_table
0x1ed8.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x1ee8: per day (1-based) the Trammel and Felucca phase glyph characters '0'..'7'

name: draw_sky_strip_frame
purpose: Draws the empty frame of the sun/moon strip on the top text row: selects window 0; unless the location is Ararat (0x19) or g_party_z >= 0x80 (Underworld/basement), sets the cursor to column 5, row 0, draws the left end cap (draw_bar_left_cap), prints 12 spaces (string at 0xa3e2) and the right end cap (draw_bar_right_cap); then restores the previous window. draw_sky_strip later overwrites the 12 cells from column 6. Called by the map loaders MAINOUT_81d0 and TOWN_85d8.

name: draw_bar_left_cap
purpose: Draws the left end cap of a UI bar at the current text cursor: computes the cell's pixel origin (x=(win.x0+cursor_col)*8, y=(win.y0+cursor_row)*8), saves the window attribute byte, sets text colour g_ui_color2 and background 0, prints glyph 2 of the current font (which advances the cursor), then in g_ui_color1 draws two line segments (x,y)-(x+5,y+3) and (x+5,y+4)-(x,y+7) forming a '>' outline over the glyph, and restores fg (attr&0xf) / bg (attr>>4). Used by draw_status_window, set_wind_and_draw, the sky strip, the status icon and titles, DUNGEON/INTRO/MAINOUT/TOWN/COMBAT/SHOPPES.

0x5364.name: g_text_window_attr
0x5364.meaning: window record +6: fg (low nibble) / bg (high nibble) attribute

name: draw_bar_right_cap
purpose: Mirror image of draw_bar_left_cap: prints glyph 1 of the current font in g_ui_color2 on black at the cursor, then in g_ui_color1 draws (x+7,y)-(x+2,y+3) and (x+2,y+4)-(x+7,y+7) (a '<' outline), restoring the window's fg/bg attribute afterwards.

name: str_index_of
proto: int str_index_of(const char *s /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, unsigned char ch /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Returns the index of the first occurrence of ch in the NUL-terminated string s, or the string length if ch does not occur (also returns the index of the NUL when ch==0). Used by BLCKTHRN, ENDGAME, OUTSUBS and ZSTATS for parsing/formatting.

name: draw_status_icon_bar
purpose: Draws the small bar that holds the status icon between the party list and the food/gold lines of the right-hand status window: fill_rect(240,81,263,86) in g_ui_color2, then horizontal lines y=80 and y=87 from x=240 to 263 in g_ui_color1 (pixel rows 80..87 = text row 10, columns 30..32). draw_status_icon then prints the icon character in the middle. Callers: CAST d712 and several ZSTATS screens.

name: draw_status_icon
purpose: Prints one character between bar end caps at text column 30, row 10 of window 0 (the status-icon slot drawn by draw_status_icon_bar): saves the current window, selects window 0, set_cursor_pos(30,10), draw_bar_left_cap, put_char(ch), draw_bar_right_cap, restores the window. ZSTATS passes g_status_icon (save 0x2D4: 'T' time stop, 'Q' quickness, protection icons...).

name: draw_status_top_bar
purpose: Draws the plain top bar of the right-hand status window: fill_rect(192,0,311,6) in g_ui_color2 and draw_hline(192,7,311) in g_ui_color1. Used to clear a title drawn by draw_status_title (callers: select_party_member, CAST, CMDS, SHOPPES, ZSTATS).

name: draw_status_title
purpose: Draws a centred title in the top bar of the status window. n = str_len(title); start column c = 30 - n/2. Fills the bar to the left of the title (x 192 .. c*8) and to the right (x (c+n+2)*8 .. 311) over y 0..6 in g_ui_color2 with g_ui_color1 lines at y=7 under each part, then selects window 0, set_cursor_pos(c,0), draw_bar_left_cap, print_string(title), draw_bar_right_cap, and restores the previous window. The title with its caps therefore occupies columns c..c+n+1, centred on column ~31 (x 248). Callers: select_party_member (2d7a), CAST, CMDS, SHOPPES, ZSTATS.

name: clear_status_separator
purpose: Erases the separator bar below the party list in the status window: draws vertical lines at x=191 and x=312 for y 56..63 in g_ui_color1 (the window's side borders) and fills x 192..311, y 56..63 with colour 0 (black). Counterpart of draw_status_separator; used when a screen (ZSTATS, CAST, CMDS, SHOPPES3) needs that row for text.

name: draw_status_separator
purpose: Draws the separator bar between the party list and the food/gold/date lines of the status window: fill_rect(191,57,312,62) in g_ui_color2 and horizontal lines y=56 and y=63 from x=192 to 311 in g_ui_color1 (text row 7). Called by draw_status_window (2900) and the screens that restore the normal layout.

name: pass_time
purpose: Advances the game clock by `minutes` and recomputes the light level. (1) If minutes != 0: under the 'Q' status icon (Quickness) minutes >>= 1 (min 1); g_hour_prev = g_hour; unless the icon is 'T' (time stop): g_minute += minutes and the torch (g_torch_turns) and light-spell (g_light_spell_turns) counters are decremented by minutes (floor 0). If g_minute > 59: minute -= 60, g_hours_until_heal -= 1 (floor 0), hour++. If hour > 23: hour = 0 and a new day starts: each of the 3 Shadowlords (g_shadowlord_loc, < 0x80 = not destroyed) moves to a random town rand_range(1,8) that is neither the party's current location nor any Shadowlord's current town (re-rolled until valid); day++. If day > 28: the three g_harvest_day bytes, g_skull_key_day and g_unk_5959 are zeroed, day = 1, every character record's months-at-inn (+0x17) is incremented while < 25, month++, and if month > 13 month = 1 and g_year++. draw_status_window() after any hour change. (2) Light (skipped if g_light_level > 0x32): in Ararat (0x19), when g_party_z >= 0x80, or when hour < 5 or hour > 19 the level is 2 (night: only the 3x3 around the party); hour 5 uses g_dawn_light_table[minute/10] (2,5,10,20,34,49) and hour 19 the same table with (59-minute)/10 (dusk); other hours 0x32 (full view). Then a light spell forces at least 0x12 and a torch at least 10. If the level changed, g_view_dirty = 1. (3) If the hour changed from g_hour_prev: draw_sky_strip() when not in a dungeon and not in the underworld, and g_clock_chimes = hour mod 12 (12 at midnight). (4) In a settlement (1..0x20) calls ROOT 71aa (driver entry 36 with AX=2, BL=hour, BH=minute - a time-of-day hook in the driver, see part 4). 19 callers (all main loops, camping, combat...).

0x587a.name: g_status_icon
0x587a.meaning: save 0x2D4 status icon: 'T' time stop, 'Q' quickness

0x58a5.name: g_light_level
0x58a5.meaning: save 0x2FF light intensity = max squared view distance (2 night .. 0x32 full)

0x588c.name: g_hours_until_heal
0x588c.meaning: save 0x2E6 hours until camping heals again

0x58c8.name: g_shadowlord_loc
0x58c8.meaning: save 0x322 town (1..8) of each Shadowlord, 0xff destroyed

0x5858.name: g_harvest_day
0x5858.meaning: save 0x2B2 day each nightshade/mandrake spot was harvested

0x57b2.name: g_skull_key_day
0x57b2.meaning: save 0x20C day skull keys were last taken

0x55bf.name: g_party_months_at_inn
0x55bf.meaning: character record +0x17, all 16 records, capped at 25

0x6a80.name: g_dawn_light_table
0x6a80.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a90: light level per 10 minutes of dawn/dusk: 2,5,10,20,34,49

0x24e6.name: g_view_dirty
0x24e6.meaning: set to 1 when the light level changes

0x5884.name: g_clock_chimes
0x5884.meaning: strikes to sound = hour on a 12-hour clock

notes: Driver entry 36 is called via 71aa (part 4). Month 13 exists (13-month calendar).

name: random_sitting_frame
purpose: Returns 0 while time is stopped (g_status_icon == 'T'), otherwise rand_range(0,3). Used by place_object_in_view to pick the animation frame of a creature that is eating at a table, in the stocks/manacles or reflected in a mirror.

name: place_object_in_view
proto: void place_object_in_view(int col /*param_5,[bp+c]*/, int row /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, int x /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int y /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int tile /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Stores an object/creature sprite (tile is 0x100-relative) into view cell (row,col) for map position (x,y), applying the furniture/terrain substitutions. Fast path: if tile is not a creature-like sprite (0x1c avatar on foot, 0x12-0x15 mounted party, 0x28-0x2b skiff, or >= 0x40 NPC/monster) it is stored as is. Otherwise under = *get_map_tile(x,y): 0xec (standard of Britannia) or 0x0a (tropical forest) -> return, the creature is hidden; 0x57 (a crenellation) -> g_view_tiles[row][col] = 0x38 (gargoyle statue) and return (nothing stored in the object layer: gargoyles perched on the wall look like statues); 0x6a/0x6b (bridge over a river) -> sea monsters (tile & 0xf0 == 0x80) and skiffs (tile & 0xfc == 0x28) are hidden under the bridge, others stored as is. For tiles < 0x80 (people) further substitutions: chair 0x92 -> if the tile south (x,y+1) is a table with food 0x9a or 0x9c, tile = 0x34 + random_sitting_frame() (eating), else 0x32 (seated); chair 0x90 -> if north (x,y-1) is 0x9b/0x9c, 0x38 + frame else 0x30; chairs 0x91/0x93 -> 0x30 + (under & 3); stocks 0x84 -> 0x60 + frame, manacles 0x85 -> 0x64 + frame (prisoners); mirror 0x9d/0x9e -> 0x3c + frame; bed 0xab -> 0x1a (occupied bed); ladders 0xc8/0xc9 -> 0x17/0x18. If no substitution matched and the tile north of the creature is a mirror 0x9d and row > 0, the view cell above (g_view_tiles[row-1][col]) is set to 0x9e (mirror showing a reflection). Finally g_view_objects[row][col] = tile and g_view_tiles[row][col] = 0 (meaning 'draw the object layer here'). Only caller: place_objects_in_view.
notes: 0x5c-based tiles (0x15c musician) are translated before the call by place_objects_in_view. Sitting frame groups: 0x130-0x133 occupied chair, 0x134-0x13b eating, 0x13c-0x13f 'trapped soul' (mirror), 0x160-0x167 prisoners.

name: place_objects_in_view
purpose: Merges the monster/object table into the 11x11 view. Outside combat it first stores the party into slot 0 (x,y,z from g_party_x/y/z, tile0 = anim tile = g_transport_tile) and applies a distance rule to the view terrain: a cell holding 0xdd (a 'parched desert' variant) whose squared distance from the centre (view_dist_sq, 6ff0) is > 5 becomes plain desert 0x1c, and a 0x1c cell within distance 5 becomes 0xdd (something in the desert that is only visible close up - presumably the sand-trap marking). Then for every slot from 31 down to 0 with tile0 != 0: outside combat the slot must be on the party's level and within the view (col = x-(px-5), row = y-(py-5), both <= 10); in combat col=x,row=y. The slot is skipped if its anim tile is 0 or the view cell is 0xff (dark) or 0x87 (archway - things under an arch are hidden). Then: fields (tile0 & 0xfc == 0xe8) and corpses (tile0 0x1e/0x1f) are stored only if the cell has no object yet (view != 0); anim tiles 0x1d/0x1e always overwrite the cell (object = anim tile, view = 0); a musician (tile0 == 0x5c) standing on chair 0x92 is stored as itself, otherwise drawn as anim tile - 8 (the 0x154 merchant-like sprite) through place_object_in_view; everything else goes through place_object_in_view(col,row,x,y,anim_tile). Since lower slots are processed last, slot 0 (the party) wins conflicts. Callers: refresh_map_view, CAST c6cc, CAST2 e64c.

0x587c.name: g_transport_tile
0x587c.meaning: party sprite (0x1c foot, 0x10 horse, 0x14 carpet, 0x20 frigate, 0x28 skiff)

0x5c5a.name: g_monster_table
0x5c5a.meaning: slot 0 = party; loop runs from slot 31 (0x5d52) down to 0

notes: Meaning of tile 0xdd vs 0x1c is inferred (both named 'parched desert' in LOOK2.DAT).

name: combatant_side
purpose: Returns which side a combat-roster entry fights on: 0 = party side, 1 = enemy side. flags = g_combat_roster[index].+2: if bit 5 (0x20, out of combat/dead/fled) is set -> 0. If bit 7 (party member) is clear (a monster) -> 1 unless bit 0 (charmed) is set. For a party member: if the member index (+3) is nonzero and the 5th character of that member's name (record +4) is 'j' - i.e. the name is 'Saduj', the traitor - the result is always 1; otherwise bit 0 (charmed) gives 1, else 0. draw_map_view only draws the turn highlight for side 0; COMBAT uses it to decide friend/foe when choosing targets.

0xba16.name: g_roster_flags
0xba16.meaning: g_combat_roster +2 flags: 0x80 party member, 0x20 inactive, 0x10/0x04 (COMBAT), 0x01 charmed; stride 8

0xba17.name: g_roster_member
0xba17.meaning: g_combat_roster +3: party member index / monster type

0x55ac.name: g_party_name4
0x55ac.meaning: character record +4 (5th name letter); 'j' identifies Saduj

notes: The 'j' test is the Saduj traitor check (S-a-d-u-j).

name: draw_map_view
purpose: Renders the 11x11 view buffers to the screen. For each cell (row 0..10, col 0..10): if g_view_tiles[row][col] == 0 the object layer is drawn: draw_tile(0x100 | g_view_objects[row][col], col, row) unless the object byte is 0x16 (sprite 0x116, blank - the cell is left untouched, used while the party is 'invisible' during moongate effects); otherwise if the terrain is 0xdc (moon gate) and 1 <= g_moongate_height <= 15 it draws the partial gate with draw_effect_frame(height, col, row), else draw_tile(g_tile_anim_map[terrain], col, row) (0xff draws the darkness tile). In combat (g_location >= 0x80) it then toggles g_focus_blink every frame and, when it is now nonzero, g_active_combatant != 0xff and combatant_side(active) == 0, draws a 2-pixel thick square (lines at the cell's edges, pixel rect x*16+8 .. x*16+23) around the active combatant's cell (x,y from roster +6/+7) in g_ui_color1; and if g_crosshair_visible it draws the targeting crosshair at cell (g_crosshair_x, g_crosshair_y): four corner brackets made of short line segments in g_ui_color1 with black (0) lines alongside. Callers: refresh_map_view, CAST, CAST2, LOOKOBJ.

0x589f.name: g_focus_blink
0x589f.meaning: save 0x2F9: toggled each frame; highlight/crosshair drawn when 1

notes: Exact crosshair geometry: two nested loops of draw_line/draw_line_to around (cx*16, cy*16) offsets 10..15; reproduce from the code if pixel-exact output is needed.

name: refresh_map_view
purpose: The per-frame map update called from read_command_key and ~50 other places. Sets g_disk_drive_set = 0xff (forces re-selection of the drive on the next file access). If the status icon is 'T' (time stop) g_animate_flag = 0. If g_map_update_enabled: when g_animate_flag != 0: if it is not 0xff run animate_monsters(); random_wind_change(); and outside combat update_moongates() and ROOT 70a6 (part 4, a light-level-gated animation of a special object pair at 0x217e..0x2186). Then outside combat: if g_view_dirty == 0 only the view cells that are 0 (where objects were drawn last frame) are refilled from the map (get_map_tile(px-5+col, py-5+row)); otherwise build_lit_view(g_light_level, px-g_chunk_x, py-g_chunk_y, 11) rebuilds the whole view with line of sight and g_view_dirty = 0. In combat the 11 rows x 32 bytes of the combat map (g_light_map/0xad14) are copied into g_view_tiles. Then place_objects_in_view(); draw_map_view(); and if g_animate_flag != 0 play_ambient_sounds(). Finally g_animate_flag = 1 (0xff = 'redraw only' is a one-shot).

0x545e.name: g_disk_drive_set
0x545e.meaning: disk whose drive letter is selected; 0xff = none

0x5891.name: g_animate_flag
0x5891.meaning: save 0x2EB: 0 skip animation this frame, 1 animate, 0xff redraw without monster animation

name: flood_visibility
proto: void flood_visibility(int radius /*param_7,[bp+10]*/, int y0 /*param_6*/, int x0 /*param_5*/, int row_base /*param_4; -111 = view mode*/, int col_base /*param_3*/, int stride /*param_2, unused*/, u8 *dest /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Breadth-first line-of-sight flood over the 11x11 view area. (x0,y0) is the map position of view cell (0,0) relative to the chunk origin (get_map_tile is called with (x0+col+g_chunk_x, y0+row+g_chunk_y)). dest[(row_base+row)*0x20 + col_base + col] receives the result; the stride argument is ignored (0x20 hard-coded). Two modes: row_base == -111 (0xff91) selects VIEW mode (called by build_lit_view with dest = g_view_tiles, row_base becomes 0); any other value is LIGHT-MAP mode (called by rebuild_light_map with dest = g_light_map and row/col_base = source-5, g_view_tiles used as a scratch 'visited' grid). Algorithm: a 256-entry queue of (row,col) on the stack starts with the centre (5,5), whose dest cell is set to the map tile; pop cells and visit the 8 neighbours in order W,SW,S,SE,E,NE,N,NW, skipping those outside 0..10. A neighbour is skipped if already visited: view mode: dest cell != 0xff; light mode: g_view_tiles cell == 0 or row_base+row > 31, else it is marked by writing 0. For a visited cell: tile = map tile, d = view_dist_sq(row,col). If d <= radius the cell is lit: dest = tile. Otherwise, view mode: if the tile is opaque (tile_transparent(d,tile) false) it is shown (dest = tile) only when the queue-head cell's dest is nonzero AND both the parent and this cell are lit in g_light_map, else dest = 0xff (dark) and tile = 0xff; if transparent it is shown when the cell lies in the 32x32 map and g_light_map says it is lit, else dest = 0 (dark). Light mode beyond radius: tile = 0xff, nothing written. Finally if tile_transparent(d, tile) the cell is pushed so the flood continues through it (windows/doors with windows are transparent only when adjacent, d == 1). Net effect: everything within the light radius plus anything lit by a map light source that has an unobstructed path is visible.

0xab02.name: g_view_tiles
0xab02.meaning: dest in view mode / visited grid in light mode

0xad14.name: g_light_map
0xad14.meaning: 0 = unlit, else lit (tile value) - consulted in view mode, written in light mode

0x6aa8.name: g_view_dist_sq
0x6aa8.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6ab8: squared distance from the view centre for one quadrant (mirrored by view_dist_sq 6ff0): 0 at (5,5) .. 50 at the corner

0x6a86.name: g_opaque_tiles
0x6a86.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a96: tiles that block sight (trees 09/0a, mountains 0c/0d, walls 4d-4f, 5a, odd door 97, doors b8/b9, fireplace bc, d0-d3, f8, wall fe, darkness ff) - used by tile_transparent (5dfe)

notes: Helper semantics (6ff0 = view_dist_sq(row,col) returning g_view_dist_sq for the mirrored quadrant, 0 outside 0..10; 5dfe = tile_transparent(dist_sq, tile): tiles 0x4a arrow slit, 0x4b window, 0xba/0xbb doors with window, 0x98 odd door transparent only when dist_sq == 1, otherwise transparent iff not in g_opaque_tiles) belong to part 4 but were read to make this description. The opaque-beyond-radius rule in view mode depends on dest cells of the queue head being nonzero, i.e. already shown.

name: build_lit_view
proto: void build_lit_view(int light /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, int px_rel /*param_3*/, int py_rel /*param_2*/, int size /*param_1, always 11, unused*/)
purpose: Rebuilds g_view_tiles from the map around the party. (px_rel,py_rel) = party position minus the chunk origin. Fills the 11x11 view with 0xff (darkness). If light > 0: flood_visibility(light, py_rel-5, px_rel-5, -111 (view mode), 0, 0x20, g_view_tiles), then every view cell still 0 (visited but dark) becomes 0xff. If light < 0 (only reachable from CAST2 e64c): the 11x11 cells are copied straight from the map (full visibility, no line of sight). light == 0 leaves everything dark. Called by refresh_map_view when g_view_dirty is set.
